reason: While the text mentions that the Israelites will serve (תַּֽעַבְדוּן) God on the mountain, it does not present worship to Yahweh as the defining characteristic that makes the Hebrews a people. Instead, the text establishes their identity through ancestral lineage (God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob) and God's covenantal claim on them as 'my people' (עַמִּי). Worship is presented as a future obligation resulting from God's rescue, not as the constitutive element that makes them a people.
